response.explanation: The added test repeats the existing date-override query with the same UTC start and end times and a different viewer timezone (Asia/Dhaka). It expects the same UTC slots, which matches its comment. The Timezones map defines "+6:00", and the assertion helper is used the same way as in the first assertion.
response.title: No defect found in added timezone assertion

response.consequence: Valid slots disappear from getSchedule for hosts with more than one availability range on a day. Slots that end after closing time are still offered, because the end bound is never checked against the slot end.
response.explanation: In checkIfIsAvailable, `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` (the same expression as `start`), not from `slotEndTime`. A slot that starts inside working hours but runs past `endTime` is therefore never rejected. The check also uses `workingHours.find(...)` and returns 'outside' as soon as any single entry for that weekday fails `start < startTime || end > endTime`. A day with split availability, such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, produces two entries. A 14:00 slot is outside the first entry (`end > 720`), so `find` matches and the function returns false. The slot is dropped even though it lies inside the second range. The same split-range problem affects overlapping or multi-range availability for any user.

other_findings.consequence: A zero-length override is not treated as blocking through this branch. It relies on the later isBefore/isSame/isAfter checks, which may not cover the case.
other_findings.explanation: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two freshly created objects with `===`, so it is always false. The intended zero-length override (day marked unavailable) case is never handled by this branch.
